key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskite solar cells, locating preferential degradation at the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive optical screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface UV damage and improving stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence excitation.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL and ideality-factor measurements during UV soaking.
Compare perovskite films and p-i-n devices with different indium tin oxide surface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements identified preferential buried-interface degradation consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, while interface modification improved UV stability in both films and devices.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains, and validation beyond UV soaking remains necessary.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
